items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: oh I can’t remember who the guys were but it’d be people like Larry Carlton

ctx.x: You’ve heard of this? Oh. Well anyway there were several of these movies. One of them, this particular one, was called “The Soul of Nigger Charlie,” it was a western, right, in which the hero was a black man who had problems. Okay. So there were several songs that Lou was going to record and one of them was called “Sunshine Day.” Well this was arranged by a guy named Don Costa, who was a very well-known musical director and arranger for the movies, and it was done at MGM studios in Los Angeles, and I was brought…

lesson learned there is that once you’ve done a work for hire, they can do whatever they want with it. They can use it, they can not use it, whatever. So I said jeez, it was a good solo, wasn’t it? It was a good experience, it just didn’t come out in public that way. So I got myself on the movie screen and on the radio.
